request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (50,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `utilization`: revolving credit utilization: the share of the credit limit in use (0 to 1).
  Share of importance 34.7% (95% band 32.5% to 37.9%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.189: -0.8; 0.189 <= x < 0.374: -0.44; 0.374 <= x < 0.501: -0.158; 0.501 <= x < 0.609: +0.1; 0.609 <= x < 0.666: +0.8; 0.666 <= x < 0.71: +1.4; 0.71 <= x < 0.762: +2.2; 0.762 <= x < 0.818: +2.8; x >= 0.818: +3.8 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +3.40, 95% band [+3.06, +3.51]).
- `n_delinquencies`: number of past delinquencies on the credit file (0 to 6).
  Share of importance 20.6% (95% band 18.7% to 22.5%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.2; >= 2: +0.6 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.95, 95% band [+0.82, +0.99]).
- `income`: annual income in US dollars.
  Share of importance 11.7% (95% band 9.9% to 12.6%); rank 3 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 25,000: +0.5; 25,000 <= x < 46,600: +0.204; 46,600 <= x < 59,200: -0.05; x >= 59,200: -0.25 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.81, 95% band [-0.93, -0.64]).
- `history_months`: length of the credit history in months.
  Share of importance 8.8% (95% band 7.6% to 10.1%); rank 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 58.3: +0.266; 58.3 <= x < 190: +0.059; x >= 190: -0.16 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.50, 95% band [-0.67, -0.43]).
- `dti`: debt-to-income ratio (0 to 0.6).
  Share of importance 7.2% (95% band 5.5% to 7.6%); rank 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.446: -0.07; x >= 0.446: +0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.37, 95% band [+0.24, +0.43]).
- `n_inquiries`: number of recent credit inquiries.
  Share of importance 1.7% (95% band 0.4% to 3.0%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.11 (95% band [+0.02, +0.19]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 4 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `feature_b`: an application attribute (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.5% (95% band 0.2% to 2.3%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.02, 95% band [-0.14, +0.06]).
- `feature_a`: an application attribute (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.2% to 1.7%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.01, 95% band [-0.06, +0.08]).
- `age`: age of the applicant in years.
  Share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.1% to 1.5%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 70.8: 0; x >= 70.8: +0.11 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.01, 95% band [-0.09, +0.07]).

Interactions: the model has 34 pairs. The larger ones:
- `utilization & history_months`: share of importance 1.3% (95% band 0.6% to 2.1%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0978 to 0.749: +3.40 (95% band +3.03 to +3.53) when `history_months` = 23.5, +3.45 (95% band +3.03 to +3.57) when `history_months` = 342.
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.5 to 342: -0.59 (95% band -0.81 to -0.38) when `utilization` = 0.0978, -0.54 (95% band -0.73 to -0.31) when `utilization` = 0.749.
- `utilization & n_delinquencies`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.9% to 2.4%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0978 to 0.749: +3.41 (95% band +3.06 to +3.53) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, +3.37 (95% band +2.99 to +3.58) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: +0.87 (95% band +0.70 to +0.97) when `utilization` = 0.0978, +0.83 (95% band +0.63 to +1.04) when `utilization` = 0.749.
- `utilization & income`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.9% to 1.8%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0978 to 0.749: +3.57 (95% band +3.02 to +3.60) when `income` = 21,900, +3.28 (95% band +3.01 to +3.55) when `income` = 114,000.
  Effect of `income` from 21,900 to 114,000: -0.71 (95% band -1.05 to -0.52) when `utilization` = 0.0978, -1.00 (95% band -1.08 to -0.65) when `utilization` = 0.749.
- `income & history_months`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.5% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `income` from 21,900 to 114,000: -0.84 (95% band -0.99 to -0.62) when `history_months` = 23.5, -0.79 (95% band -0.91 to -0.49) when `history_months` = 342.
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.5 to 342: -0.53 (95% band -0.87 to -0.44) when `income` = 21,900, -0.48 (95% band -0.70 to -0.34) when `income` = 114,000.
- `utilization & dti`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.4% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0978 to 0.749: +3.38 (95% band +2.99 to +3.49) when `dti` = 0.0295, +3.47 (95% band +3.02 to +3.62) when `dti` = 0.571.
  Effect of `dti` from 0.0295 to 0.571: +0.28 (95% band -0.04 to +0.51) when `utilization` = 0.0978, +0.38 (95% band +0.22 to +0.48) when `utilization` = 0.749.
- `n_delinquencies & income`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.3% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: +0.90 (95% band +0.77 to +0.98) when `income` = 21,900, +1.00 (95% band +0.83 to +1.05) when `income` = 114,000.
  Effect of `income` from 21,900 to 114,000: -0.85 (95% band -1.01 to -0.65) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, -0.75 (95% band -0.90 to -0.58) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
- `n_delinquencies & feature_b`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.0% to 0.8%).
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: +0.97 (95% band +0.80 to +0.99) when `feature_b` = -1.64, +0.91 (95% band +0.81 to +1.00) when `feature_b` = 1.63.
  Effect of `feature_b` from -1.64 to 1.63: +0.00 (95% band -0.15 to +0.05) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, -0.05 (95% band -0.16 to +0.08) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
- `n_inquiries & feature_b`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.0% to 0.6%).
  Effect of `n_inquiries` from 0 to 4: +0.05 (95% band +0.01 to +0.19) when `feature_b` = -1.64, +0.13 (95% band +0.02 to +0.24) when `feature_b` = 1.63.
  Effect of `feature_b` from -1.64 to 1.63: -0.04 (95% band -0.16 to +0.06) when `n_inquiries` = 0, +0.04 (95% band -0.13 to +0.10) when `n_inquiries` = 4.
- 26 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 5.4%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"Revolving credit utilization is by far the strongest driver of predicted default: applicants using a small share of their credit limit receive a substantially lower predicted risk, and the risk climbs steeply as utilization rises above about 0.6, with the net effect from the 5th to the 95th percentile of utilization being roughly +3.4 on the log-odds scale."},{"id":2,"text":"The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver: having no delinquencies lowers predicted risk, one delinquency raises it slightly, and two or more raise it further, with a net effect of about +0.95 across the typical range."},{"id":3,"text":"Income matters mainly at the low end: applicants earning under about $25,000 carry higher predicted risk, while those above about $59,000 carry lower predicted risk, a net effect of about -0.8 across the typical range."},{"id":4,"text":"Length of credit history and debt-to-income ratio play smaller but consistent roles: a short history (under roughly 58 months) and a high debt-to-income ratio (above about 0.45) each push predicted risk up, while very long histories (over about 190 months) push it down."},{"id":5,"text":"The interactions are modest in size: the effect of utilization is slightly weaker at higher incomes, and the effect of delinquencies is slightly stronger at higher incomes, but these shifts are small compared with the main effects of utilization and delinquencies."},{"id":6,"text":"Recent credit inquiries have only a small upward effect on predicted risk, and the data do not resolve the shape of that effect between the lowest and highest counts."},{"id":7,"text":"The two standardised application attributes (feature_a and feature_b) and applicant age have effects that the data do not distinguish from zero, so they should not be read as drivers of the model's predictions."}]}
